bull_bear.body: Prioritizing organic capacity expansion (oral solids, injectables) and inorganic M&A in niche segments. Dividend: INR 1 final + INR 2 special (total INR 3/share). Strong FCF (INR 958cr) supports aggressive growth capex without debt.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 1) API Price Volatility: Cephalosporin and bulk API prices remain below peak levels, pressuring API segment profitability. 2) Geopolitical/Crude: Inflation in solvents/raw materials (though largely pass-through). 3) Execution Risk: Delays in EU commercialization or Zambia facility commissioning. 4) Regulatory: Schedule M implementation pace and inspection outcomes.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and pragmatic. Acknowledged FY26 as 'transitional' with H1 challenges but emphasized strong Q4 momentum. Clear focus on long-term value creation via regulated markets over short-term trade generic scale. Transparent on API losses and path to recovery.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The Trade Generics business was consciously shrunk to fix working capital cycles, not due to lack of demand; it is now a small, profitable niche. The EUR 200mn EU contract is for an established molecule with predictable volumes, de-risking the ramp-up. The Zambia deal includes a transition from export (FY27-28) to local manufacturing (FY29+), locking in long-term sovereign demand.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Objects-of-the-offer table shows the IPO proceeds fully deployed as on June 30, 2026, with the unutilized amount shown as "-" against every object.
- Stated objects and amounts (INR Cr, offer document = utilization): repayment of borrowings of Akums 159.91; repayment of borrowings of subsidiaries 227.09; funding incremental working capital 55.00; pursuing inorganic growth initiatives through acquisitions 30.18; general corporate purposes 170.00.
- The Rs 56 Crore Oriflame purchase is presented as in line with the stated inorganic-growth strategy of improving positioning and augmenting margins.
- Managing Directors state they "remain committed to creating long term shareholder value".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Largest India-focused CDMO by revenue, production capacity and clients served
- Long-standing partnerships with 26 of the top 30 pharmaceutical companies in India and 1,400+ CDMO clients
- Ownership of intellectual property for several manufacturing processes and deep formulation/process expertise
- Large, growing in-house R&D capability (370+ scientists, 1,192 patents granted cumulatively, R&D spend at 3.2% of revenue) supporting new-formulation development
- Global regulatory accreditations (WHO-GMP, EU-GMP) enabling access to regulated international markets
- Diversified presence across the pharmaceutical value chain (CDMO, branded formulations, API) providing multiple growth levers while mitigating single-segment risk
- Pan-India distribution network reaching urban and rural geographies
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Global trade friction, tariff shifts and geopolitical realignment — The MD&A's Global and Indian Economy overview repeatedly flags renewed trade frictions, geoeconomic fragmentation, evolving geopolitical developments and potential supply-side disruptions as sources of continued global uncertainty; Akums is actively expanding its export and international footprint (Europe, Africa/Zambia) and is therefore exposed to these external headwinds.
- Commodity price volatility and global supply-chain disruption — The Indian Economy Outlook explicitly names commodity price volatility and global trade uncertainties as potential headwinds to India's growth trajectory, and the Global Economy section separately flags potential supply-side disruptions; both are relevant to Akums as an API/formulations manufacturer dependent on input costs and cross-border logistics.
- Elevated public debt and fiscal pressure in advanced economies constraining global demand — Cited in the Global Economy overview as a headwind to sustained global growth and monetary policy flexibility, which could dampen demand conditions in Akums' developed-market (European) expansion markets.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

Recent API price hikes (single high-digits) benefit absolute margins despite soft YoY comparison. Gross margins supported by shift to complex dosage forms and regulated markets. Operating leverage from capacity utilization driving EBITDA expansion.

outlook.body: Revenue: CDMO double-digit volume growth expected in H1 FY27; Domestic Formulations to grow at/above IPM (high single/low double digit); International Formulations to return to double-digit growth. Margins: CDMO margins to sustain ~13-14%; API losses to reduce sizably but may remain negative for full year FY27. Order Inflow: Zambia supplies commence Q2 FY27; EU commercial supplies from FY28. Capex: INR 300cr targeted for FY27.

outlook.body: Zambia: $25mn per annum for FY27 & FY28 (supplies from India), followed by local manufacturing ramp-up from FY29. EU CDMO: EUR 35mn per annum for 6 years (till 2032), commencing FY28. Domestic CDMO: Strong pipeline with 10+ products for European markets.

outlook.body: 1) Zambia JV: $45mn total capex (51% Akums), local production from FY29 targeting $200mn market. 2) EU Regulated Markets: Plant 2 accredited, dossier filing underway for 10+ products, commercial supply FY28. 3) Injectables: New facility ramping up (teens utilization), expected significant contribution in FY27. 4) Inorganic M&A: Evaluating niche business acquisitions using strong cash reserves.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Deepen core CDMO strengths and expand high-value/complex dosage capabilities (sterile injectables, hormones, beta-lactams) to capture premium outsourcing mandates and enhance margins through complex offerings
- Expand international/regulated-market footprint through Europe (EU-GMP accredited plants, first major European CDMO formulation mandate) and Africa (Zambia joint venture) to shift from a domestic manufacturer with export exposure toward a global CDMO partner
- Drive an innovation-led product pipeline via strengthened R&D, continued DCGI approvals, first-to-market and complex launches, and increased filings in regulated markets to drive portfolio premiumisation
- Improve utilisation of newly ramped manufacturing capacities and drive scale efficiencies across sterile, oral solid and liquid dosage forms
- Embed sustainability into the manufacturing ecosystem — standardise ESG-aligned sourcing practices, implement vendor performance analytics, integrate logistics with emissions monitoring, and enhance ESG disclosures
- De-risk geographic concentration by creating a regional export hub for Southern Africa and strengthening relationships with sovereign institutions
- The Board recommended a final plus special dividend for FY2025-26, payable out of the Company's profits and subject to shareholder approval at the AGM, indicating an intent to return a portion of profit to shareholders alongside continued reinvestment in the core manufacturing and CDMO business (organic capacity expansion and international JV/expansion activity) in the ordinary course of business; no separate, more detailed dividend-distribution-policy statement (e.g., a target payout ratio) is present in this bundle beyond the specific FY2025-26 recommendation.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Akums operates 14 consolidated manufacturing facilities (11 CDMO plants and 3 API plants), clustered at Haridwar and Kotdwar (Uttarakhand) and Baddi (Himachal Pradesh) for CDMO/formulations, and at Sundran and Chachrauli (Punjab) and Barwala (Haryana) for API. During FY2025-26 the Company commenced operations at a new injectable manufacturing facility in Haridwar, strengthening sterile manufacturing capabilities, and ramped up newly commissioned Oncology and Steroid facilities. Consolidated CDMO capacity utilisation improved steadily from 24.6% in FY2023-24 to 39.4% in FY2024-25 and 42.9% in FY2025-26, while the API business operated at utilisation levels of 50%-84%; overall consolidated capacity utilisation stood at ~47%, which management said gives significant headroom to grow without substantial incremental capital investment. A total capital expenditure of Rs.2,220 Million was deployed during the year towards capacity expansion, equipment modernisation, infrastructure upgrades and regulatory compliance initiatives, with the largest share (Rs.519.07 Million) directed to the Akums-3 facility to strengthen production capabilities, install advanced manufacturing equipment and enhance operational efficiency. The Company also reported a ~15% productivity improvement during FY2025-26. Separately, during the year the Company entered into a Joint Venture with the Government of the Republic of Zambia for the establishment of a pharmaceutical manufacturing facility, marking a strategic step in its global expansion.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural industry shift from conventional generics to complex and differentiated dosage forms (sterile injectables, modified-release formulations), driven by pricing pressure in standard categories and rising demand from biologics, oncology and GLP-1 pipelines
- Patent expiries worth USD 63.7 Billion between 2025-2029 creating a significant opportunity for complex generic development
- Regulatory upgrades such as India's revised Schedule M framework accelerating quality-led industry consolidation, favouring manufacturers with advanced infrastructure and compliance capabilities
- Outsourcing becoming structurally embedded in global pharmaceutical value chains, supporting continued CDMO demand
- Sustained growth in global and Indian healthcare/wellness consumption: global pharmaceutical market projected to grow at an 8.19% CAGR to CY2034; Indian IPM reached Rs.2.42 lakh crore as of January 2026, growing 8.0% YoY with monthly growth accelerating to 10.21%
- CDMO business delivered double-digit volume growth in FY2025-26, significantly outpacing broader IPM volume growth, with CDMO contributing 80% of total revenue
- Participation in high-growth chronic therapies (cardiology, anti-diabetics, CNS, gastroenterology) through Akumentis Healthcare, and in the wellness segment through a US-NSF certified nutraceutical facility
- 10+ products in pipeline for European filings until FY28
- CEP filings initiated for select APIs
- Government of Zambia procurement commitment of USD 25 Million per annum for FY27 and FY28, providing a demand-assured gateway for the Zambia joint venture
- Progress on the European CDMO contract with commencement of commercial supplies (Dapagliflozin and Rivaroxaban) to Europe/Switzerland

deepdive.thesis: Akums navigated a challenging H1 FY26 to deliver strong Q4 recovery, driven by double-digit CDMO volume growth and the turning of Trade Generics EBITDA positive, while setting up significant optionality via a $25mn/year Zambia sovereign contract and EU commercial supplies starting FY28. The key inflection is the expected sharp reduction in API losses and the transition from domestic dependency to high-margin regulated market exports.

wtt.tone_latest: Confident, recovery-toned; management framed FY26 as a 'transitional year', owned the API business as 'a year of miss', and pointed to double-digit H2 volume momentum and margin normalization while declining to give an FY27 top-line number.

meta.thesis: Akums navigated a challenging H1 FY26 to deliver strong Q4 recovery, driven by double-digit CDMO volume growth and the turning of Trade Generics EBITDA positive, while setting up significant optionality via a $25mn/year Zambia sovereign contract and EU commercial supplies starting FY28. The key inflection is the expected sharp reduction in API losses and the transition from domestic dependency to high-margin regulated market exports.
